newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks cut gains on Dow slide.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks cut gains on Dow slide.

text.p: Mexican stocks had pared virtually all earlier gains in slow mid-afternoon trading Friday due to a downtrend on Wall Street, traders said.

"We managed to ignore the Dow this morning because of the public finance data, but it is weighing heavily," a desk trader said, referring to first quarter public finance figures announced by Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz on Thursday.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was up 2.04 points, or 0.05 percent, at 3,889.24. Trading volume .TV.MX was dull at 46.1 million shares.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 79.12 points at 7,254.43.
"The market is quite slow, there are some foreign buyers but they are very selective. Everyone is waiting for Monday's data," the trader added.

The Finance Ministry will release first quarter GDP on Monday. Ortiz told journalists yesterday that he expected first quarter growth of 4.5-5.0 percent. This compares with 5.12 percent growth predicted in a Reuters survey MEX22.
Telmex weighed most on the downside, accounting for some 18 percent of all shares traded, and was off two centavoss at 17.12 pesos. The telecomms stocks' ADRs were meanwhile off 3/8 to 43-1/4.
Blue chips were mostly buoyed up by financial group Bancomer, up four centavos to 2.95 pesos.
On the broad market, of 91 stocks traded, 41 were up while 34 were down.
